description: D4(a), the positive half — retire hand-curation into ingest and REDIRECT the curation budget to the one thing nobody publishes (docs/DECISION-D4-CLDF-AND-WIKIBASE.md §2-3). Hand-curating 1,099 languages (data/source/lexicons/languages.tsv) and 543 families (families.tsv) against Glottolog's published ~8,600 language-level languoids is the largest avoidable cost in the repo, and docs/corpus-tier-report.md already shows the cost is not buying quality: only 552/1,099 language rows and 0/543 family rows are QID-anchored + reference-backed. Once 113 has landed the Glottolog substrate, the curated spine is superseded for everything Glottolog publishes — identity, genealogy, codes, classification — and every hour spent maintaining it is an hour not spent on the CROSS-DOMAIN LINEAGE DAG (cuisine / religion / genetics / trade x language), which no CLDF dataset, no CLLD instance, and no other open project publishes. That DAG is pinakes's actual differentiator, and it is currently the least-resourced part of the corpus. This tasklist executes the swap: audit what the curated rows still add over the ingest, retire the rest into the ingested substrate WITHOUT losing a single genuinely-curated value, install a guard so the spine cannot silently re-grow by hand, and stand the lineage DAG up as a first-class curated artifact with its own schema, coverage target, and report. Nothing here is a deletion of information — it is a change of AUTHORITY over which column comes from where. Scope: the language/family lexicons, the curation policy docs, the convergence-QA guard, and the lineage-DAG schema + report.

userStories.title: Audit the curated spine against the ingested substrate
userStories.description: Before retiring anything, produce the evidence: for every curated language and family row, what does it hold that the Glottolog ingest does not? The output is a committed delta report that makes the retirement decision reviewable rather than assumed.
acceptanceCriteria: A committed delta report (docs/, generated by a script under scripts/) classifies every row of languages.tsv and families.tsv against the ingested Glottolog substrate as: SUPERSEDED (every non-empty cell is matched or bettered by the ingest), ADDITIVE (carries at least one field Glottolog does not publish — e.g. curated `historical_context`, `time_origin`/`time_end`, `native_speakers`, `endangerment_status`, or a curated `sources` citation), or UNMATCHED (no Glottolog counterpart at all — reconstructed, historical, or dialect-level rows the catalogue does not cover), with per-class counts and per-field evidence.

The report names, field by field, which columns Glottolog is authoritative for after the swap and which stay curated, and that mapping is written into docs/canonical-schema.md (or docs/ATTRIBUTION.md, whichever the field's authority belongs in) so the answer is documented rather than folklore.
The report is regenerable and pinned by a test; `.chief/verify.sh` passes.

userStories.title: Retire the superseded rows into the ingest without losing a curated value
userStories.description: Execute the swap for the SUPERSEDED class: the ingested substrate becomes the authority for identity/genealogy/codes/classification, curated ADDITIVE fields survive as an overlay on the ingested row, and UNMATCHED rows stay curated because nobody publishes them.
acceptanceCriteria: Every row the US-1 report classified SUPERSEDED derives its identity, glottocode/ISO codes, parent/family genealogy and classification from the ingested Glottolog record rather than a hand-maintained cell — and a test asserts that no cell value present before the swap and NOT published by Glottolog was dropped in it (the ADDITIVE overlay is preserved verbatim, provenance included).

UNMATCHED rows (reconstructed proto-languages, historical variants, dialect-level entries Glottolog does not carry) remain curated and are explicitly labelled as such in the corpus, so the residual curation surface is a known, countable set rather than an unbounded backlog — its size is recorded in the coverage report.

`bun run convergence-qa` is green with the dedup-ratchet and attribution gates re-baselined only where counts legitimately moved, every pinned snapshot the change cascades into is regenerated per scripts/CLAUDE.md, and `.chief/verify.sh` passes.

userStories.title: Guard the retirement and stand up the lineage DAG as the curated artifact
userStories.description: Make the swap durable — hand-added languoid rows that duplicate published CLDF content are caught by a gate, not by review vigilance — and redirect the freed curation budget by making the cross-domain lineage DAG a first-class artifact with a schema, a coverage target, and a report.
acceptanceCriteria: A convergence-QA check fails when a new languages.tsv / families.tsv row is added by hand that a published CLDF release already covers (matched by glottocode/ISO/name against the ingested substrate), pointing the contributor at the ingest path instead — proven by a test that adds such a row and asserts the gate fires; the check permits UNMATCHED-class additions with an explicit marker.

The cross-domain lineage DAG (cuisine / religion / genetics / trade x language, over the existing DESCENDS_FROM / INFLUENCED_BY / DERIVED_FROM edge vocabulary) is defined as a first-class curated artifact: its node/edge shape stated in docs/, a committed coverage report giving the current cross-domain edge counts per domain pair, and a stated target — so the differentiator has a number attached to it for the first time.

The repo's curation guidance (CLAUDE.md invariants + docs/ATTRIBUTION.md 'How to Add New Data Sources') states the new rule plainly: what a published CLDF release covers is INGESTED, never hand-curated; curation is spent on the cross-domain lineage DAG and on the UNMATCHED residual.
`.chief/verify.sh` passes and the new report regenerates deterministically.
